sections.title: The letter i
paragraphs: The letter is called (i) /i/. Its main sound appears in the word (isola) /ˈiːzola/, which means island. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter can make two sounds, and it can also be silent.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue very high. Keep your tongue pushed forward near the roof of your mouth. For the glide sound, make the same shape but glide quickly into the next vowel. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake for both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling and sounds
paragraphs: This letter sounds like the vowel in (amici) /aˈmiːtʃi/ when it stands on its own. It sounds like a quick glide in (piatto) /ˈpjatto/ before another vowel in one beat. The letter is not pronounced in (ciao) /ˈtʃaːo/, where it only changes the sound of the letter before it.

sections.title: Comparing with English
paragraphs: Do not say this vowel like the short sound in bit or sit. Keep your tongue high and tense, like the vowel sound in meet. In words where the letter is silent, do not add an extra sound. Keep the word smooth without inserting an extra glide.
